messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — High error rate detected for customer MapleHealth (dedicated pool us-west-2-pool-12). Errors: 502/503 spike across inference pods. Trigger: error_rate > 5% for 2m. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1234
Aisha Kaur: I’m on it, pulling logs now. Any customer-facing pages already? Maya, are they in the loop?
Maya (Customer Success): Not yet — I can open a hello message if this is going to be >15m. Maples’ engineers are on standby.
Aisha Kaur: quick triage: errors originate from one AZ in us-west-2, nodes in pool-12 showing OOMs in nginx proxy before model. Could be a kernel-level memory fragmentation causing nginx worker crashes. Attaching recent logs.
Aisha Kaur: ```
[2024-05-03T14:02:11Z] nginx[pid:2345]: worker process 2348 exited on signal 9
[2024-05-03T14:02:12Z] containerd: oom-kill: pid=2348 comm=\"nginx: worker\"
[... repeated across pods: pool-12-node-[3,7,9]]
```
Riley Chen: If it's OOM on proxy, we can spin up a temporary proxy-only replica set and drain traffic off the failing nodes. Are the failing pods pinned to a host label?
Aisha Kaur: Yes, pool-12 is a dedicated pool with custom host labels. I’m going to cordon node-3 and drain gracefully. Planning: 1) cordon node-3 2) scale pool-12 proxy replicas +2 3) route MapleHealth traffic to fallback pool-7 (compatible model variant) while we stabilize.
Luis Ortega: Agree. Also suggest enabling prefix KV-cache bypass for MapleHealth while we triage to reduce memory pressure. That will increase token cost but reduce per-request memory.
Aisha Kaur: Executing now. Commands:```
# cordon and drain
kubectl cordon pool-12-node-3 -n redwood-serving
kubectl drain pool-12-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-serving
# scale proxy
kubectl scale deployment/redwood-proxy-pool-12 --replicas=6 -n redwood-serving
# route override for MapleHealth
redwoodctl routing override --customer maplehealth --to-pool pool-7 --duration 30m
```
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: routing override (user: Aisha Kaur). Rollout id: ro-7890.
Aisha Kaur: Done cordon + drain on node-3. New proxy replicas launched, CPU/mem stable so far. Redirecting MapleHealth traffic to pool-7.
incident-bot: Route override completed. Observability: error rate for MapleHealth has dropped from 7.2% to 0.4% in the last 2m.
Maya (Customer Success): I sent a short message to MapleHealth: "We observed elevated errors affecting your dedicated pool. We've routed traffic to a healthy fallback and are stabilizing. No action required on your side. We'll follow up with a detailed timeline." They replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted"
Riley Chen: I'll keep monitoring memory metrics + kernel logs. If crashes persist, plan B is to provision a new dedicated pool and migrate live connections — that's heavier but minimizes cross-tenant risk.
Luis Ortega: Also flagged potential kernel bug on the node image version (ubuntu-5.15-custom). I'll open infra ticket to validate kernel & docker runtime.
Aisha Kaur: Triage summary so far: Impact: MapleHealth requests in pool-12 experienced 502/503 from 14:01–14:08 UTC. Mitigation: cordon/drain node-3, scale proxy, route to pool-7 at 14:09. Recovery: error rate normalized by 14:12. Incident declared resolved for customer traffic at 14:12, but infra investigation ongoing.
Daniel Park: Thanks — can you paste a short 2-3 line exec summary I can use for the customer exec update and for our SLA review? Also need impact window and whether credit is owed per MapleHealth contract (SLA: 99.9% per-month; they lost estimated 7m of availability on their dedicated pool).
Maya (Customer Success): I have their contract open — if we count the minutes where routing was degraded (14:01–14:09), that's 8 minutes of increased error rate. Per SLA formula that may not trigger a credit, but we should still offer goodwill credit.
Aisha Kaur: Exec summary draft: "At 14:01 UTC we detected elevated 502/503 errors affecting MapleHealth's dedicated inference pool (pool-12) due to OOMs in the nginx proxy on a subset of nodes. We cordoned and drained the affected host, scaled proxy replicas, and temporarily routed traffic to a healthy fallback pool; service returned to normal by 14:12 UTC. We are investigating a candidate kernel/runtime issue and will provide a full RCA and remediation plan."
Daniel Park: Good. For the post-incident comms email I'll expand with timeline bullets and next steps. Maya, can you confirm whether they want an upstream exec call?
Maya (Customer Success): They asked for a 30m sync if the RCA indicates service-level causes. Hold for RCA draft — I'll propose Wednesday 16:00 PT if needed.
Luis Ortega: Infra ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4567 — investigating kernel OOM behavior and kubelet/cgroup settings. Assigning to infra team.
Riley Chen: One more note — we observed elevated connection count from MapleHealth proxies during the spike which may have exhausted worker threads. We should add a per-tenant connection limit for proxies on dedicated pools as a mitigation. Filing a config change PR.
Aisha Kaur: Handoff to next oncall: @Riley Chen — I'll leave follow-ups (kernel logs, postmortem draft) for you. Key artifacts: routing override ro-7890, infra ticket INFRA-4567, logs attached to INC-1234.
Riley Chen: Taking over. My plan: validate kernel OOM evidence, run node repro (stress test), and draft RCA. ETA for initial RCA draft: 2024-05-04 18:00 UTC.
Daniel Park: From a comms perspective: short customer note done, exec summary approved (Aisha draft). I'll draft the public-facing apology + SLA/credit proposal: offer one month of service credit equivalent to MapleHealth’s monthly dedicated pool fee as goodwill (subject to approvals).
finance-bot: Noted request for credit approval. Please submit via billing workflow: https://billing.redwood.internal/credits/new with INC-1234 attached.
Maya (Customer Success): Submitted to billing, referenced INC-1234 and proposed goodwill credit.
Aisha Kaur: Closing notes: immediate mitigation saved customer traffic with minimal exposure. Root cause investigation underway; next steps: 1) infra kernel/runtime patch or rollback; 2) add per-tenant connection cap; 3) add automated mitigation playbook to route-to-fallback for dedicated pools; 4) customer RCA + offer.
Riley Chen: I'll attach the RCA draft in this thread when ready. If anyone has logs or notes to add, paste them here.
Maya (Customer Success): Thanks everyone — will update MapleHealth after RCA draft and coordinate exec call if needed. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-1234 marked as customer-impact mitigated (maplehealth) at 1714800720. Ongoing: investigation.
Luis Ortega: Adding final note for post-incident: schedule a dedicated-runbook review with infra + serving runtime next week to ensure node image and kube settings are hardened for dedicated pools.
Daniel Park: Thanks team — good quick coordination.
Riley Chen: (RCA draft will be here)
